title: US 224 over Eight Mile Creek | retained bridge with proposed 2026 repairs
source_note: Primary INDOT B-44532 / Des2200957 proposed 2026 repair set, document 9683628. Retained CB21 section and supports are checked against unchanged supplementary 1985/1986 B-16317 plans, document 9548292. Revision9707311 changes closure time only.
assumptions: Exterior visualization reconstruction of the named design state, not an as-built survey, structural rating or validated finite-element mesh.
No internal reinforcement, prestressing strands, embedded anchors or fabrication holes. Colors identify visualization layers; amber parts identify explicit approximations.
Source PDF page references always address drawings.pdf, an unchanged issued PDF. Supplemental historical pages are separately identified by document ID and local file.
Constructed interfaces and bearing contact checks establish geometric attachment only. Surveyed seats, actual camber, shim thicknesses and installed tolerances remain unknown.
Site terrain, channel solids, riprap individual stones, buried pile tips, full roadside guardrail terminals and nonstructural utility routing are omitted.
Latest primary coping width controls the 5 in discrepancy with historical revised slab width.
Native Z uses an illustrative 817 ft flowline datum; source grade and nominal beam contacts are reconstructed, not surveyed.
Void geometry is included to prevent a solid rectangular visual section from being mistaken for a hollow box. FEM section properties still require independent explicit calculation.

source_index.note: Primary drawings.pdf is byte-for-byte identical to the issued source; no combined or newly authored PDF. Supplemental page numbers do not address the primary PDF.

completeness: Whole crossing reconstructed with unresolved detail (amber)

detail_coverage.detail: One 41 ft bearing span, six hollow CB21 beams at 7 ft 9 in, 30 degree left skew; 7.5 in remaining slab and separate proposed 2 in overlay. North is +Y, left of increasing station, and the north end of each abutment is down-station (sheets 7, 8; reflected in revision 1.2).
Twelve retained Type 7B bearing envelopes, end/interior concrete diaphragms, both solid abutments, shallow footings and four flared wings. Historical source is explicitly supplemental.

All twelve beam ends receive nominal wrap skins; reconstructed mudwalls, PCF strips, two approaches, three TFC transition envelopes, and retained midspan drain outlets. TFC sections follow sheet 12 C-C to F-F; mid-span drains are open 2 in cores through the slab (sheet 9; revision 1.2).
Actual deterioration and patch boundaries, wrap properties, bearing standard PB11 dimensions, slab/beam camber, wing outlines, guardrail terminals, full drainage and site geometry.

known_deviations.deviation: Wings A (northwest) and D (southeast) remain straight 4.70 m walls at 30 deg to the abutment with the top at about El. 831.15 (A) / 830.96 (D) at the tip, 1.15 / 1.12 m above the drawn tips. Elevation F-F gives 23 ft 10 1/2 in: level El. 831.65 (Abut. 1) / 831.47 (Abut. 2) for 4 ft 10 3/4 in, then falling over 18 ft 11 3/4 in to El. 827.38 / 827.30, with a root leg along the railing; sheet 10 removes part of the wing top under the new RCBA extension.
known_deviations.reason: Needs a rebuild of the kinked historical outline reconciled with the 2026 removals, beyond a correction.

known_deviations.deviation: At the NW and SE corners sheet 12 has a new 5 ft 9 5/8 in Type FC railing on the existing wingwall from the PCF joint, a 1/4 in open joint, then the 15 ft 8 in TFC, so those TFCs and their RCBA extensions (the outer about 15 ft 10 in of the 20 ft 6 in slab edge, sheets 13-14) lie about 1.4 m farther from the bridge than modelled, and the 5 ft 9 5/8 in railings are missing. At the NE corner the new 7 ft 10 5/8 in railing replaces the last 6 ft 9 in of the existing railing on the deck (sheet 10) and the modelled TFC start is within a few cm.
known_deviations.reason: Requires new railing components and shortened retained rails, beyond a correction.

known_deviations.parts: deck, overlay, retained_coping_-1, retained_coping_1, mudwall_1, mudwall_2, PCF_joint_-1, PCF_joint_1
known_deviations.source: sheet 10 Section E-E, sheet 11 Section C-C, sheet 15
known_deviations.deviation: The deck, overlay and copings run to the 45 ft 0 1/2 in floor end over the 1 ft reconstructed mudwall, and the PCF joint is drawn at the mudwall back face; the drawings put the joint at the span face of the mudwall, whose top is flush with the overlay and the RCBA. The concealed mudwall top is flat (111 mm below the crown at Line A).
known_deviations.reason: The visible floor surface is at the correct crowned elevation; correcting the arrangement means shortening the deck, overlay and copings and moving the joints, beyond a correction.

known_deviations.deviation: Wings B (southwest) and C (northeast) start at the generator's abutment-cap end, 0.15 m outside the coping line; at 60 deg to the abutment their 0.40 m wall stands 50 mm clear of the deck edge at the root. 1985 sheet 5 (plan) starts the wing's inner face at the coping corner on the abutment front face, and the wall is 1 ft thick at the top, battered to 1 ft 9 1/2 in (End Elevation B-B).
known_deviations.reason: Placing the root needs the wing/abutment junction rebuilt with the historical cap outline, as for the acute-corner wings; a shift to close the gap alone would not follow the drawings.

known_deviations.deviation: The overlay keeps its full surface up to the 2 in drain cores; sheet 9 tapers the surface down to the existing drain edge over 1 ft 0 in toward the drain (a 1 ft x 2 ft area at each drain).
known_deviations.reason: The depth of the taper ("to Ex. Drain Edge") is not dimensioned.
